supersedes: tier0-v0.2.json, for the two TRANSPORT objects only
notes: A new versioned artifact rather than an edit. tier0-v0.1.json and tier0-v0.2.json remain exactly as published: historical conformance vectors are never rewritten to make newer code look compatible.

TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT gained a 32-bit migration_ref, so their bytes changed. TRANSPORT_OFFER is 13 -> 17 bytes and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT is 12 -> 16 bytes. The Tier-0 maximum was already 17 (REQUEST), so the correlator cost no additional maximum size.

WHY migration_ref EXISTS: without it, a delayed TRANSPORT_ACCEPT belonging to an abandoned offer is indistinguishable from the acceptance of the current one, because transport_id and profile_id are normally identical across a retry. The peer would migrate on the strength of a stale acceptance. CoAP carries a Token echoed by the responder, and MCTP keeps its message tag separate from endpoint addressing, for the same reason.
migration_ref correlates one transport-change transaction. It is not identity, not authorization, not a session reference, and not a secret. Zero is reserved.
The other five Tier-0 layouts are byte-identical to v0.1 and v0.2 and are repeated here so this file is a complete set.
transport_id values are assigned by mcl-link/registries/transport-ids-v0.1.json: 1 MCL_AP, 2 MCL_IP, 3 MCL_BLE, 4 MCL_UWB. Both transport vectors below use 2 = MCL_IP.
Do not infer transport assignments from vector provenance; see the warning in tier0-v0.2.json.
